answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small stake in a shared vault before it may trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Reputation then accrues per identity like layers of pigment on a ridge: each honest transaction adds a visible, durable mark, while a single fraud wipes the layer clean and forfeits the stake. The vault refunds the stake only after a long clean-history window, so short-lived sock puppets gain nothing while honest agents climb cheaply on proven records.
